sentences: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is treated with a combination of antibiotics to cover the most likely pathogens, including Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, anaerobes, Gram-negative facultative bacteria, and streptococci
The treatment regimen typically includes a combination of a cephalosporin and doxycycline, with or without metronidazole

For outpatient treatment, a common regimen is ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly in a single dose, plus doxycycline 100 mg orally twice a day for 14 days, with or without metronidazole 500 mg orally twice a day for 14 days
For inpatient treatment, one option is cefotetan 2 g intravenously every 12 hours or cefoxitin 2 g intravenously every 6 hours, plus doxycycline 100 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours
Patients should be re-evaluated within 48-72 hours to ensure clinical improvement
Sexual partners should also be treated to prevent reinfection
